title: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo Leg Review: Five Distances in the City of Love
seo_title: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo Review | Philippines
meta_description: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo leg review: September 20 -- five distances from 1K to 21K, part of a bank-backed series that drew 14,000 runners in 2025.
dek: Set for 20 September 2026 in Iloilo City, this leg of the EastWest Dream Run series brings the same 1K-to-21K distance spread and bank-backed production seen at the Clark leg to the historic 'City of Love.'
verdict: The Iloilo leg of the EastWest Dream Run carries the same strengths as its Clark counterpart covered elsewhere in this batch: a genuinely strong series debut (roughly 14,000 runners nationwide in 2025), bank backing from EastWest Bank, and an unusually wide five-distance spread from 1K to 21K that suits families and first-timers alongside serious half-marathon runners. Iloilo City itself is one of the Philippines' oldest and historically significant cities -- regional capital of Western Visayas, once the country's second most important city after Manila. Registration status for this specific leg isn't yet announced, so it's a step behind some of the series' other 2026 stops in terms of confirmed logistics.

sections.heading: The Same Wide Distance Spread as Clark
paragraphs: The Iloilo leg offers five distances -- 1K, 3K, 5K, 10K and 21K -- the same format used at the Clark leg of this series. [1] That range makes it one of the more genuinely inclusive races in this research batch, suiting everyone from a family fun-run to a competitive half marathon within a single event.

sections.heading: A Bank-Backed Series With a Strong 2025 Debut
paragraphs: The overall EastWest Dream Run series debuted in 2025 and drew around 14,000 runners nationwide, organised by RunRio in partnership with EastWest Bank. [1] That scale and financial backing typically translates to solid production values -- race villages, amenities, and marketing reach -- even for legs, like Iloilo's, that are newer additions to the series.

sections.heading: Iloilo City: 'La Muy Leal y Noble Ciudad'
paragraphs: Iloilo City is the regional centre of Western Visayas and one of the oldest cities in the Philippines. Granted city status by royal decree in 1889 with the honorific 'La Muy Leal y Noble Ciudad,' it had become the second most important city in the Philippines after Manila by the late 19th century. [2] Today it's known as the 'City of Love,' with a compact administrative core across seven districts -- a genuinely rich historical backdrop for a race weekend.

sections.heading: Registration Not Yet Announced
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status for the Iloilo leg has not been announced. [1] Given the series' overall popularity and the Clark leg's own tight registration timelines noted elsewhere in this research, it's worth monitoring RunRio's official channels closely rather than waiting for a formal opening announcement.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a bank-backed, well-resourced race with genuine distance-range flexibility in one of the Philippines' most historically significant cities, the EastWest Dream Run's Iloilo leg on 20 September 2026 is a strong pick once registration opens. Keep an eye on official channels, since sign-up details weren't yet confirmed at the time of this research.
